- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.4) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward surprise.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model overcorrects in next period; reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- If true price deviates from 30-day moving average by >2%, model often fails to revert; apply mean reversion bias toward prior 10-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2 or vice versa), adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift, not just price history.
- Model tends to lag in low-sentiment periods; if sentiment drops below 0.4, forecast should be adjusted downward by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- In high-sentiment periods, model often overestimates early; apply a 1–2% downward correction to first 5–7 forecast points to avoid premature peak.
